en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on the Great Chariot (Mahārathavagga)
7. The Second Mansion Story on What Should Be Done “High is this mansion with its jeweled pillars,
extending twelve yojanas in every direction.”
Seven hundred lofty gabled chambers,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with golden ornaments;
there you eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.
And divine lutes play their sweet melodies;
here are the five strands of sensual pleasure with divine flavors,
and women adorned in gold dance.
“By what means do you have such a complexion...
[as before] ...and your complexion illuminates all directions?”
Thus the son of the gods was delighted...
[as before] ...the fruit of which action this is.
“Meritorious deeds should be performed by the wise person who understands,
toward monks who have attained the right path.”
Wherein what is given bears great fruit.
Truly, for my benefit, O bhikkhu,
you have come from the forest to the village.
Having inspired confidence there in my mind,
I went to the realm of the Thirty-three;
because of that, such is my complexion.
"...and my radiance shines in all directions.
Thus ends the seventh *Vimāna*, the Second *Karaṇīya*.
